name: Creature Battle Simulator
concept_focus: Nested dictionaries and turn logic, then types, status, teams, an AI rival and finally classes

story.title: The Beast-Tamers' League
story.client: Warden Kesh of the Beast-Tamers' League
story.hook: The League's champion has not lost a battle in nine seasons, and Kesh suspects the arena itself favours them. Build an honest battle simulator, rule by rule, then build the rival who can actually beat the champion.

acts.title: Act I: First Blood
acts.goal: One creature, one attack, misses, and turns that alternate.

acts.title: Act II: The Duel
acts.goal: Move menus, an enemy that chooses, a clean end at 0 HP and readable battle text.

acts.title: Act III: The Trainer
acts.goal: Types, status effects, a team of three and a rival that thinks about damage.

acts.title: Act IV: The League
acts.goal: Levels, a rewrite into classes, and a gauntlet of trainers with saved teams.

boss_lore: The Champion knows every type matchup by heart. It does not need luck; it needs you to forget one.
boss_brief: Bring a finished battle.py: creatures as a class with moves, types and status effects, teams of three with switching, an enemy that picks moves by expected damage, levels and XP, and a gauntlet of trainers with your team saved between runs.
boss_twist: The Arena Champion brings a type you did not plan for. Keep the type chart as data and add one new type to it without touching the battle logic. Write predict_winner(team_a, team_b, battles=500, seed=None) that runs seeded battles and returns both win rates, and make the enemy switch out when its active creature is at a 2x type disadvantage and below 30% HP. Status effects must expire on the right turn even when a creature switches out and back in.

twist_2.label: Phase 2: The Champion's ace evolves
twist_2.quest: The Champion's last creature evolves mid-battle. Write evolve(creature): when a creature reaches its level threshold during a battle it becomes its next form, keeping its HP percentage, current status and learned moves, and gaining the new form's stats and one new move. Show one evolution happening mid-fight in the battle log.

mobs.name: The Wild Slime
mobs.encounter: Design one creature with a name, HP, stats and a single move, and explain why each piece of data sits where it does.
mobs.contract: A slime oozes out of the tall grass. Describe it completely as data before it can do anything at all.

objectives.label: Describe the creature
objectives.brief: In battle.py, describe a creature as a dictionary with a name, HP, max HP, attack, defence and a move that is itself a dictionary.

objectives.label: Add a rival
objectives.brief: Add a second creature with the same shape and print both clearly.

objectives.label: Explain the nesting
objectives.brief: Explain why the move is a dictionary inside the creature and how you reach its power.

mobs.name: The Feral Fang
mobs.encounter: Make one attack land and reason about which creature's data changes and which stays untouched.
mobs.contract: The Fang bites. Somebody's HP goes down. Make sure it is the right somebody.

objectives.label: Write attack
objectives.brief: Write attack(attacker, defender) that works out damage from the move power, attack and defence and lowers the defender's HP.

objectives.label: Trace the damage
objectives.brief: Predict the defender's HP after one attack with your numbers, then check it.

objectives.label: Hit the right creature
objectives.brief: Explain which dictionary your function changes and why the attacker's own data must stay untouched.

mobs.name: The Miss Wisp
mobs.encounter: Give moves an accuracy so attacks can miss and explain how a random roll becomes a hit or a miss.
mobs.contract: The Wisp flickers. Half your attacks pass straight through it. Give every move an accuracy and let fate decide.

objectives.label: Add accuracy
objectives.brief: Give moves an accuracy from 0 to 100 and roll for a hit before dealing damage.

objectives.label: Measure the hit rate
objectives.brief: Roll a 70-accuracy move 1,000 times and show the hit rate is close to 70 percent.

objectives.label: Get the boundary right
objectives.brief: Explain whether your roll uses < or <= and how that changes the real hit chance.

mobs.name: The Turn Goblin
mobs.encounter: Let both sides take repeated turns and trace whose turn it is at every point in the loop.
mobs.contract: The Goblin keeps skipping its turn, then taking two. Make the turns honest: you, then it, until one falls.

objectives.label: Alternate turns
objectives.brief: Loop the battle so the two creatures attack in turn until one reaches 0 HP, with a speed stat deciding who acts first each round.

objectives.label: Trace the turns
objectives.brief: Trace who acts in the first three rounds with your two creatures, then check the battle log.

mobs.name: The Move Keeper
mobs.concept: Lists of dictionaries and menu input
mobs.encounter: Let the player pick from several moves and reject choices that do not exist.
mobs.contract: Every creature knows four moves. The Keeper makes sure you can choose any of them and none that do not exist.

objectives.label: Give four moves
objectives.brief: Give each creature a list of up to four move dictionaries with name, power and accuracy.

objectives.label: Choose a move
objectives.brief: Show the player's moves as a numbered menu and use the chosen one, asking again on bad input.

objectives.label: Guard the index
objectives.brief: Explain what happens when the player types 0 or 5 for a four-move menu, and handle both.

mobs.name: The Mindless Rival
mobs.encounter: Have the enemy choose its own move each turn and explain how it reaches into the same move data as the player.
mobs.contract: Your rival does not think yet. It flails through its own moves at random. That is still better than standing still.

objectives.label: Let the enemy choose
objectives.brief: Have the enemy pick one of its own moves at random each turn and use the same attack function.

objectives.label: Share the attack code
objectives.brief: Explain why both sides use one attack function and what would go wrong with two copies.

objectives.label: Handle an empty move list
objectives.brief: Explain what random.choice does with an empty list and make sure a creature without moves cannot crash the battle.

mobs.name: The Health Reaper
mobs.encounter: End the battle exactly when a creature hits 0 HP, keeping HP from going negative and stopping a fallen creature from striking back.
mobs.contract: The Reaper takes anyone who reaches zero. Make sure the fallen stay fallen and nobody bleeds below nothing.

objectives.label: Clamp HP at zero
objectives.brief: Never let HP drop below 0 or rise above max HP.

objectives.label: Stop the fallen
objectives.brief: End the round immediately when a creature faints, so it cannot attack after reaching 0.

objectives.label: Catch the ghost attack
objectives.brief: Explain the order bug where a creature at 0 HP still gets its turn, and show your check prevents it.

mobs.name: The Battle Bard
mobs.concept: String formatting and fresh state per battle
mobs.encounter: Make battle text and remaining HP readable, then explain how a new battle starts at full HP instead of carrying old wounds.
mobs.contract: The Bard sings of every battle, but nobody can follow the verses. Make the text clear and let each new battle start whole.

objectives.label: Write the battle text
objectives.brief: Print each action clearly with damage, misses and an HP bar made of characters for both creatures.

objectives.label: Heal between battles
objectives.brief: Start every new battle with both creatures at full HP, copying their starting data instead of reusing it.

objectives.label: Explain the copy
objectives.brief: Explain why assigning a creature dictionary to a new name does not copy it, and how you make a real copy.

mobs.name: The Type Oracle
mobs.encounter: Add types and a type chart that makes moves strong or weak.
mobs.contract: Fire burns grass, water drowns fire. The Oracle keeps the whole chart. Without it every battle is just a contest of numbers.

objectives.label: Write the chart
objectives.brief: Give creatures and moves a type, and build a dictionary of dictionaries with the damage multiplier for each attacking and defending type.

objectives.label: Apply the multiplier
objectives.brief: Multiply damage by the chart and print super effective or not very effective.

objectives.label: Trace a matchup
objectives.brief: Predict the damage of one strong and one weak matchup with your numbers, then check.

mobs.name: The Venom Moth
mobs.encounter: Add poison and sleep that last a few turns.
mobs.contract: The Moth's dust poisons slowly and puts you to sleep. Status lingers between turns, and something has to count it down.

objectives.label: Add status effects
objectives.brief: Let moves inflict poison (damage at the end of each turn) or sleep (skip turns), each with a number of turns left.

objectives.label: Count them down
objectives.brief: Apply and count down every effect at the right point in the turn, and remove it when it runs out.

objectives.label: Stop the stacking
objectives.brief: Explain what should happen when poison lands on an already poisoned creature, and make your code do that.

mobs.name: The Pack Leader
mobs.encounter: Battle with teams of three, switching and sending the next one when one faints.
mobs.contract: Nobody battles the League with one beast. Lead a pack of three, swap them when it helps, and send the next when one falls.

objectives.label: Field a team
objectives.brief: Give each side a list of three creatures with one active at a time.

objectives.label: Switch creatures
objectives.brief: Let the player switch the active creature as their turn, and send the next living creature in when one faints.

objectives.label: End on a wiped team
objectives.brief: End the battle only when every creature on one side has fainted, and say who won.

mobs.name: The Cunning Rival
mobs.encounter: Make the enemy pick the move with the highest expected damage.
mobs.contract: Kesh's best rival thinks before it strikes. For every move it asks: how hard would this hit, how likely is it to land?

objectives.label: Estimate each move
objectives.brief: Write expected_damage(attacker, move, defender) from power, type multiplier and accuracy, without dealing any damage.

objectives.label: Pick the best move
objectives.brief: Make the enemy use the move with the highest expected damage, and switch out when it is badly outmatched.

objectives.label: Prove it is smarter
objectives.brief: Run 200 battles of the cunning rival against the random one and explain the result.

objectives.label: Read the status
objectives.brief: Make expected_damage account for status effects (an asleep defender cannot dodge, a burned attacker hits softer) and show the rival changing its pick because of one.

mobs.name: The Growth Spirit
mobs.encounter: Award XP after battles and grow creatures as they level.
mobs.contract: A creature that never grows is a creature that will lose. Feed it victories and watch it rise.

objectives.label: Award XP
objectives.brief: Award XP to the creatures that fought, based on the level of what they beat.

objectives.label: Level up
objectives.brief: Level up at XP thresholds, raising stats, and handle gaining several levels at once.

objectives.label: Check the thresholds
objectives.brief: Explain why a big XP reward can skip a level if you only check once, and show your loop handles it.

mobs.name: The Shapeshifter
mobs.encounter: Turn creature dictionaries into a Creature class with methods.
mobs.contract: Your beasts have outgrown their dictionaries. The Shapeshifter teaches them a new form: a class that carries its own behaviour.

objectives.label: Write the class
objectives.brief: Write a Creature class whose __init__ sets its stats and moves, with methods take_damage, is_fainted and heal.

objectives.label: Battle with objects
objectives.brief: Move the battle over to Creature objects and keep every earlier feature working.

objectives.label: Explain the change
objectives.brief: Explain what got easier and what got harder when the data and its behaviour moved into a class.

mobs.name: The League Clerk
mobs.encounter: Face a series of trainers and keep your team between runs.
mobs.contract: The League is not one battle; it is a ladder of trainers, each harder than the last. The Clerk keeps your team on file between visits.

objectives.label: Climb the ladder
objectives.brief: Pit the player against a sequence of trainers with stronger teams, healing between battles.

objectives.label: Save the team
objectives.brief: Save the player's team (levels, XP, moves) to a JSON file and load it on start.

objectives.label: Open the league
objectives.brief: Add a menu: start the gauntlet, battle a random rival, view your team, or quit.

objectives.label: Counter the climber
objectives.brief: Give each trainer on the ladder a signature type, and make the next trainer counter the type your team has used most so far.
